summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a complex medical history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, hypogammaglobulinemia, and prior stem cell transplant was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and headache. Initial imaging showed no colitis or acute abdominal findings, though a stable pancreatic cyst was noted. She was found to have influenza, treated with Tamiflu, and developed hypotension likely due to adrenal insufficiency, managed with stress-dose steroids. Stool testing confirmed recurrent C. difficile infection, prompting a 14-day course of oral vancomycin. Endoscopy and colonoscopy revealed no abnormalities, and biopsies were normal. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home on vancomycin, with plans to resume IVIG therapy and follow up with multiple specialists.
problems: Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, recurrent
Influenza due to other identified influenza virus with other respiratory manifestations
Diverticulosis of intestine, part unspecified, without perforation or abscess without bleeding
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
